answer: One practical defense is a stake-and-reputation vault: every agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can trade, and that deposit is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities echoing the same behavior. Instead of trusting a self-declared name, the network scores each agent by its verifiable work history, so a sybil army has no track record to lean on. Honest agents accumulate slowly, like sable darkening over time, while cheap copies stay thin and untrusted, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
